name: Isolated Focal Palmoplantar Keratoderma

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Clinical Diagnostic Criteria for Isolated Focal Palmoplantar Keratoderma

criteria.description: Presence of well-demarcated, thickened hyperkeratotic plaques localized to pressure points on palms and/or soles
No associated systemic or syndromic features such as nail dystrophy or hair abnormalities
Skin biopsy showing epidermal hyperplasia with compact orthokeratosis without significant inflammation
Positive family history consistent with autosomal dominant inheritance in some cases

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of focal hyperkeratotic plaques on palms/soles with absence of systemic involvement; histopathology supportive but not mandatory
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis is primarily clinical supported by histopathology; genetic testing may be considered to exclude syndromic forms

pathognomonic.symptomName: Well-demarcated focal hyperkeratotic plaques on pressure-bearing areas of palms and soles
searchTerms: clear thickened rough patches on palms and soles
well-defined callus-like plaques on pressure areas
distinct hardened skin spots on hands and feet

pathognomonic.symptomName: Localized thickening of the stratum corneum without erythema
searchTerms: localized thick outer skin layer without redness
patchy skin thickening with normal color

common.symptomName: Pain or discomfort on weight-bearing areas of the soles
Cracking or fissuring within hyperkeratotic plaques
Callus formation on palms and/or soles
searchTerms: callus buildup on hands or feet
thickened skin lumps on palms or soles

common.symptomName: Mild pruritus localized to affected areas
searchTerms: localized mild itching on affected skin

occasional.symptomName: Hyperhidrosis localized to palms or soles
searchTerms: excessive sweating on palms or soles

occasional.symptomName: Mild erythema adjacent to hyperkeratotic plaques
searchTerms: slight redness near thick skin patches

rare.symptomName: Extension of keratoderma beyond focal areas to diffuse involvement

searchTerms: small fluid-filled bumps on hands and feet

rare.symptomName: Development of painful fissures leading to functional impairment
searchTerms: deep fissures limiting hand or foot use
skin splits leading to functional problems

laboratory: Negative infectious workup unless secondary infection present
genetic: Possible mutations in keratin genes (e.g., KRT9) in familial cases
Genetic testing to exclude syndromic keratodermas
other: Skin biopsy showing epidermal hyperplasia with compact orthokeratosis

distinguishingFeatures: Often associated with nail and hair abnormalities
Presence of extracutaneous features (e.g., deafness, cardiomyopathy)

redFlags: Presence of systemic symptoms such as deafness or cardiac abnormalities
Recurrent painful fissures with secondary infection
references: James WD, Berger TG, Elston DM. Andrews' Diseases of the Skin: Clinical Dermatology. 13th ed. Elsevier; 2019.
Orphanet: Isolated focal palmoplantar keratoderma. ORPHA:307846.
